legend: Anton came to a chocolate factory. There he found a working conveyor and decided to run on it from the beginning to the end.

The conveyor is a looped belt with a total length of 2l meters, of which l meters are located on the surface and are arranged in a straight line. The part of the belt which turns at any moment (the part which emerges from under the floor to the surface and returns from the surface under the floor) is assumed to be negligibly short.

The belt is moving uniformly at speed v1 meters per second. Anton will be moving on it in the same direction at the constant speed of v2 meters per second, so his speed relatively to the floor will be v1 + v2 meters per second. Anton will neither stop nor change the speed or the direction of movement.

Here and there there are chocolates stuck to the belt (n chocolates). They move together with the belt, and do not come off it. Anton is keen on the chocolates, but he is more keen to move forward. So he will pick up all the chocolates he will pass by, but nothing more. If a chocolate is at the beginning of the belt at the moment when Anton starts running, he will take it, and if a chocolate is at the end of the belt at the moment when Anton comes off the belt, he will leave it.

You are given the positions of the chocolates relative to the initial start position of the belt 0 ≤ a1 < a2 < ... < an < 2l. The positions on the belt from 0 to l correspond to the top, and from l to 2l — to the the bottom half of the belt (see example). All coordinates are given in meters.

Anton begins to run along the belt at a random moment of time. This means that all possible positions of the belt at the moment he starts running are equiprobable. For each i from 0 to n calculate the probability that Anton will pick up exactly i chocolates.
input: The first line contains space-separated integers n, l, v1 and v2 (1 ≤ n ≤ 105, 1 ≤ l, v1, v2 ≤ 109) — the number of the chocolates, the length of the conveyor's visible part, the conveyor's speed and Anton's speed.
The second line contains a sequence of space-separated integers a1, a2, ..., an (0 ≤ a1 < a2 < ... < an < 2l) — the coordinates of the chocolates.
output: Print n + 1 numbers (one per line): the probabilities that Anton picks up exactly i chocolates, for each i from 0 (the first line) to n (the last line). The answer will be considered correct if each number will have absolute or relative error of at most than 10 - 9.
note: In the first sample test Anton can pick up a chocolate if by the moment he starts running its coordinate is less than 0.5; but if by the moment the boy starts running the chocolate's coordinate is greater than or equal to 0.5, then Anton won't be able to pick it up. legend.ai: Anton 来到一家巧克力工厂。他在那里发现一条正在运转的传送带，并决定从起点跑到终点。
传送带是一条总长为 2l 米的环形带，其中 l 米位于地面上，且排列成一条直线。传送带在任意时刻转弯的部分（即从地板下方升到地面、再从地面返回地板下方的部分）可视为长度极短。
传送带以 v1 米/秒的速度匀速运动。Anton 将以 v2 米/秒的恒定速度沿同一方向在传送带上移动，因此他相对于地面的速度是 v1 + v2 米/秒。Anton 既不会停下来，也不会改变速度或移动方向。
传送带上零散地粘着一些巧克力（共 n 块）。它们会随传送带一起移动，不会从传送带上掉下来。Anton 很喜欢巧克力，但他更想继续向前移动。因此，他会拿走所有经过的巧克力，但不会多拿。如果 Anton 开始跑动时，某块巧克力正好位于传送带的起点，他会拿走它；如果 Anton 离开传送带时，某块巧克力正好位于传送带的末端，他就会留下它。
给定巧克力相对于传送带初始起点的位置 0 ≤ a1 < a2 < ... < an < 2l。传送带上从 0 到 l 的位置对应上半部分，从 l 到 2l 的位置对应下半部分（见样例）。所有坐标均以米为单位。
Anton 会在随机时刻开始沿传送带跑动。这意味着，他开始跑动时传送带的所有可能位置出现的概率均相等。对于每个 i（0 到 n），计算 Anton 恰好拿走 i 块巧克力的概率。

input.ai: 第一行包含以空格分隔的整数 n、l、v1 和 v2（1 ≤ n ≤ 105，1 ≤ l, v1, v2 ≤ 109）——巧克力的数量、传送带可见部分的长度、传送带的速度以及 Anton 的速度。
第二行包含以空格分隔的整数序列 a1, a2, ..., an（0 ≤ a1 < a2 < ... < an < 2l）——巧克力的坐标。

output.ai: 输出 n + 1 个数（每行一个）：对于每个 i（从 0（第一行）到 n（最后一行）），Anton 恰好捡起 i 块巧克力的概率。如果每个数的绝对误差或相对误差至多为 10 - 9，则答案将被认为正确。

note.ai: 在第一个样例测试中，如果 Anton 开始跑步时巧克力的坐标小于 0.5，他就能捡起这块巧克力；但如果男孩开始跑步时巧克力的坐标大于或等于 0.5，Anton 就无法捡起它。由于传送带上的所有位置出现的概率相同，捡起这块巧克力的概率为 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/55d1d7955c1e59f407eb6baa7601582a54eeac4f.png)，没能捡起它的概率为 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0e79ad74cc0314b318cc094369c845c55b37c9ef.png)。
